title: Provision Route 53 A Record
scenario: Your platform team needs Route 53 A Record for pointing a hostname at an address. Write a reusable Terraform configuration that provisions it, drives every input through variables, applies the standard tags, and exports the operational identifiers.
constraints: Create exactly one resource of type aws_route53_record.
All configurable values must come from variables declared in variables.tf.
Code must pass terraform fmt conventions (2-space indents, trailing newline, no tabs).

focus.title: Complete the aws_route53_record resource
focus.todo: Add the arguments and nested blocks required for aws_route53_record.

hints.why: DNS is the public name of the system. Managing records in Terraform keeps the name, certificate and endpoint changes together.
hints.what: Complete the marked region in `main.tf`. The work is inside `resource "aws_route53_record" "this"`. Add the arguments and nested blocks required for aws_route53_record. Use the visible constraints as the checklist for names, values and references before you run the tests.
hints.when: Use Route 53 when a service needs a stable hostname or when DNS changes should be reviewed with the rest of the stack.
hints.how: Open `main.tf` and work only inside `resource "aws_route53_record" "this"`. Use this code shape: name; type; zone_id; ttl; alias { name; zone_id }. Use the already-declared references instead of hardcoded values: `var.record_name`, `var.zone_id`, `aws_cloudfront_distribution.this.domain_name`, `aws_cloudfront_distribution.this.hosted_zone_id`. Keep the block header and braces, indent nested blocks by two spaces, and add one argument or nested block at a time. Run the tests after each small change so the first failure points at the next name to fix.
